output.summary: A large, feathery fern native to temperate Asia, Europe, North America and North Africa, lady fern commonly grows in damp, shady woodland. Its young fronds are edible when cooked, and Native Americans cook both the curled young fronds and the underground stems.
output.edibilityNote: Young fronds are edible after cooking; Native Americans cook both the curled young fronds and the underground stems.
